subject: Private GPU runway, scaling policy & network saturation test plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>

Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Subject: Private GPU runway & saturation test plan for Veridian

Team —

Attaching a first-pass plan for Veridian Health's private VPC deployment. Key asks in this thread: confirm throughput math, network assumptions, and a test schedule for a controlled saturation run in their staging VPC. High-level numbers to validate:

- Target sustained throughput: ~120k tokens/min (across pool) for steady-state ML inference (avg response ~1.8k tokens).
- Burst requirement: up to 3x sustained (~360k tokens/min) for 10 minutes to cover marketing-driven spikes.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 1200ms for responses up to 2k tokens; tail budgeted separately.
- Node requirement (ballpark): 6 A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs as a sustained baseline, 12 nodes to hit burst targets without queuing (depends on batch sizing).
- Network: assume 25 Gbps egress per pod; plan includes a single-VPC L3 path with NAT gateway for telemetry.

Areas I want team input on:
1) Network headroom calc — do we need to target 30–35 Gbps/pod to be safe once TLS overhead and retries are accounted for?
2) Autoscaler policy — prefer queue-depth + tokens/sec hybrid metric vs. pure token/sec. Thoughts?
3) Warmup strategy — suggested: pre-warm KV caches on a subset of nodes with synthetic prefixes 30m before peak window.
4) Test plan — schedule a staged saturation test (50% -> 75% -> 100% sustained; then 3x burst for 10m) and capture token/sec, p95 latency, GPU mem pressure, and network TX/RX.

Attachments: vpc-gpu-scaling-math.xlsx (estimates), runway-saturation-test-plan.md (test steps), sizing_estimates.csv (per-model token throughput).

Please review and reply with inline comments by Wednesday EOD — we need to lock the test window with Veridian and AWS next week.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine — good first pass. A few quick notes after skimming the spreadsheet: 

- Network headroom: target 35 Gbps/pod. TLS + telemetry + retries typically cost ~10–15% beyond raw model egress. If Veridian has any cross-AZ traffic or flow logs enabled, add an extra 5% buffer.
- Sizing: your 6-node baseline looks right for the model mix you called out (bert-style encoder + llama-derivative decoders). Quick local perf bench: one A100 80GB (~FP16 + 4-bit quantized path) sustained ~20k tokens/min for multi-seq patterns we care about. So 6 nodes -> ~120k tokens/min baseline; 12 nodes covers the 3x burst with headroom.
- Node churn: plan for a degraded mode where we run at 0.6x throughput per node for redistribution while machines reboot. Add a pre-scale drain window (30s) and a 2-min warmup period for new nodes.
- Observability: ensure p95 latency is correlated with per-node GPU util and network bytes/sec so we can triage whether slowdowns are compute or network.

Inline suggestions left on the spreadsheet. Also: include a brief test to simulate small-payload high-QPS traffic (50–100 tokens per response) — that'll exercise the batching and scheduling path differently.

-marcus

Quick autoscaler proposal:

- Trigger signals: combine a 60s moving average of token/sec per pool with a 90s percentile queue depth (requests waiting for a GPU slot). Require both to exceed thresholds for scale-up to avoid oscillation on microbursts.
- Scale-up policy: add 2 nodes per step, cool-down 180s.
- Scale-down policy: only after 10m of sustained low load; reduce at most 1 node per step to keep redistributes minimal.
- Warmup: when a node is added, we run a parallel warmup job that pre-populates KV caches for the top-20 customer prefixes; the node is marked ready after a 60s warmup or when a token/sec target is met.

Quantization note: if Veridian accepts an int4 path for less-sensitive models we can shave ~30% memory pressure and reduce node counts by 1–2 GPUs. Worth mentioning to procurement.

I'll update the runway-saturation-test-plan.md with autoscaler thresholds and expected timelines.

- Aditya

All — thanks for the fast turnaround. I reviewed the plan and the spreadsheet; happy to greenlight the staged soak with two small adjustments before we lock with Veridian: 

1) Increase the post-scale stabilization window to 3 minutes (from 2) to account for large-model cold-starts we've seen in preprod.
2) Add a short failback plan: if p95 latency exceeds 2x baseline for more than 3 consecutive minutes during the saturation run, immediately cut the burst to 50% and trigger emergency rollback to the previous model variant.

Next steps:
- Jasmine, confirm the AWS availability (Marcus suggested week of Jun 23).
- Aditya, update the autoscaler thresholds and doc (please link to the updated doc).
- Marcus / Soojin, prepare the observability dashboard panels (p95, token/sec, GPU util, net tx/rx) and share the Grafana link.

I've penciled a 60-minute kickoff with Veridian and AWS for Wed Jun 25 at 10:00 AM PT — here's the calendar placeholder: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=veridian-saturation-test. If that works for everyone I'll send the invite.
